name: Djinn of Ernham
notes: Known from one post to rec.sport.pro-wrestling.fantasy (1 March 1999), served at /promotions/rspwf/archive/djinn-of-ernham-looking-for-a-home-1999-03-01.html: a one-eyed Arabic brawler
caption: A one-eyed Arabic warrior who announces his invasion of the SCRA, March 1999.

name: Jon Grey

tenures.note: Calls the Free for All and the Scraps of 19 January 1998 beside Jack Hazard, hosts the Probing SCRA roundtable of 30 December 1997 and voices the Rasslefest clip show; Rock Bottom Robbie tells him "Grey, your brother better sign this one", and he says of Poink's run-in that "the president" will not like it. Aladdin Style answers what he said on Uncut about smaller wrestlers.

caption: The commentator who calls SCRA's shows beside Jack Hazard and hosts the Probing SCRA roundtable.

name: President Grey

tenures.note: The president who signs SCRA's matches: Rock Bottom Robbie tells Jon Grey "your brother better sign this one", Derek Mota says "Mr." Grey phoned to sign him, Keith Spencer says the cage match is what "President Grey gave" Lifetaker and Centris, and Nathan Flash says "President Grey pushed me into it" when he gives up the North American title.

caption: SCRA's president and Jon Grey's brother, who booked the matches his wrestlers blamed him for.

name: Jack Hazard

tenures.note: Calls the shows beside Jon Grey as the heel voice who heckles every match; in the Probing SCRA roundtable he says he gets "stuck with Grey" three times a week and listens to Ed Jaspard every Monday.

caption: The heckling second voice on SCRA's commentary desk, who works beside Jon Grey three times a week.

name: Ed Jaspard

tenures.note: Announces the Free for All matches, once starting the wrong match's introduction until the commentators correct him, and opens the Scraps of 19 January 1998 holding the vacated North American title.

caption: SCRA's ring announcer, who held the vacated North American title overhead to open the Scraps of 19 January 1998.

name: Ted Jaspard

tenures.role: Thursday-night host of the Powerhouse show
tenures.note: Keith Spencer says he holds down the Thursday-night show with Ted Jaspard; Ted storms into the Probing SCRA studio to grab Jack Hazard by the throat for mocking his tag-team partners.

caption: Keith Spencer's partner on the Thursday-night show, who dived across the Probing SCRA desk at Jack Hazard.

name: Keith Spencer

tenures.note: Guest on the Probing SCRA panel, interviews the Praetorian Guard for the ScraPreview ("I'm not paid enough for quality interviews, Tulk") and opens the Scraps of 19 January 1998 by interviewing Nathan Flash.

caption: The interviewer who questioned the Praetorian Guard before Rasslefest and Nathan Flash on 19 January 1998.

name: Raf Bullock

tenures.note: Joins the Probing SCRA panel as the Spinebuster Scoops' representative, appearing in voice and person for the first time.

caption: The Spinebuster Scoops' man on the Probing SCRA panel, who "emerges from print" to appear for the first time.

name: Tommy Gregory

tenures.role: head of security; referee of Curtis against Hardin
tenures.note: The Probing SCRA card lists him as referee of Curtis against Hardin, and the clip show calls him the new head of security who brought a fire extinguisher to ringside; Hardin warns him to stay out of the match.

caption: SCRA's head of security, named referee of the Curtis against Hardin match at Rasslefest.

name: Marty MacDonald

tenures.role: manager, called the best manager in SCRA
tenures.note: The commentators call him "the best manager in SCRA"; in the Probing SCRA picks Jack Hazard backs the Praetorian Guard because nothing "can combat MacDonald's strategy", and in the clip show Eddy Jacks grabs the microphone from him before the House of Pancakes walk out.

caption: Called the best manager in SCRA by the Free for All commentators.

name: Alexander Gudonov

tenures.note: Enters the ring ahead of the Siberian Express at the Free for All; the ScraPreview's warehouse segment has him drill two large men in the Express's moves and the commentators call him the unnamed factor in their match.

caption: The manager who drills the Siberian Express and enters the ring ahead of them.

name: Black Kat

tenures.note: Leads Prodigy to the ring for the Free for All opener, as the script notes, since she is the manager; Prodigy's ScraPreview flash says 1998 will be the year of the Kat and Prodigy.

caption: Prodigy's manager, who led him to the ring for the Free for All opener.

name: Squire Kathleen

tenures.note: Comes out from behind the curtain with Green Knight for the Free for All opener.

caption: The valet who walked Green Knight to the ring for the Free for All opener.

name: Christine

tenures.note: In Phantom's ScraPreview flash she phones Sgt. Pepper to warn him and Phantom drags her to the basement to watch tapes; Jack Hazard says Phantom is back on his list without her.

caption: Phantom's valet, who tried to warn Sgt. Pepper in Phantom's ScraPreview flash.

name: Victoria Glenn

tenures.note: Walks Bobby McAllister to the ring for his debut against Nik Nyce on 19 January 1998 and calls him over when Nyce sweet-talks her.

caption: The manager who accompanied Bobby McAllister to the ring in his debut.

name: The Creator

tenures.role: guide of the Angels of Darkness
tenures.note: Jon Grey says the Angels of Darkness "seem to be guided by the Creator"; in the clip show he orders them to show Phi Theta Kappa how they "lighten up" and Havoc calls him father.

caption: The figure who guides the Angels of Darkness and whom Havoc calls father.

name: Miss Frank

tenures.note: Grant says Tavis was in love with her and "that's the only reason she was our manager"; the clip show has the German Eagles take her from the Pros, and Keith Spencer says he prefers "Ocki".

caption: The manager whom the German Eagles took from the Pros.

name: Prodigy

tenures.role: wrestler; a Free for All winner
tenures.note: Beats Green Knight with Last Ride in the Free for All opener, led to the ring by Black Kat; his ScraPreview flash from the African jungle promises to go from co-headlining the Free for All to the main event by the end of 1998, and Aladdin Style names him the next rung on the ladder on 19 January 1998.

caption: A 276-pound Torontonian who beat Green Knight with Last Ride in the Free for All opener.

identity.note: Exact-name collision with records in other federations or on the RSPWF lists; no document on these pages ties any of them to this wing. Kept distinct under the no-merge default, open to a merge on evidence.

name: Green Knight

tenures.note: Billed from Talahassee, Florida at 200 pounds as a former TV Title holder and lost the Free for All opener to Prodigy; the commentators call him a fading star on a quick downfall.

caption: A 200-pound former TV champion on the downslide who lost the Free for All opener to Prodigy.

name: Doug "Grizzly" Adams

tenures.note: The clip show has Nemesis force him to keep attacking Phi Theta Kappa, then Adams punch Nemesis when Phi Theta Kappa offer him a place with them, setting up the match billed as the student against the teacher; on 19 January 1998 his first title shot is against Rock Bottom Robbie.

caption: Nemesis's student, who punched his manager after Phi Theta Kappa offered him a way out.

name: Nemesis

tenures.note: The clip show has him scream Adams into the ring and drag him back by the ear, then rush in after him when Adams answers Phi Theta Kappa's offer, to be punched by him ("He nailed his manager!"); the card bills the two against each other as the teacher against the student.

caption: The teacher whose student Doug "Grizzly" Adams turned on him.

identity.note: Exact-name collision with records in other federations or on the RSPWF lists; no document on these pages ties any of them to this wing. Kept distinct under the no-merge default, open to a merge on evidence.

name: Sgt. Pepper

tenures.note: Jon Grey says he is not in his September form, "when he won the TV title"; his Rasslefest opponent is Phantom, whom he is to free the league from.

caption: A technical wrestler who won the TV title in September 1997 and faced Phantom at Rasslefest.

name: Phantom

tenures.role: wrestler; a Beyonder and a former North American champion
tenures.note: Called a Beyonder and a former North American champion who has "disappeared from the scene" since losing the title; his ScraPreview flash is a gothic castle scene in which he keeps Christine in the basement.

caption: A Beyonder and former North American champion matched with Sgt. Pepper at Rasslefest.

identity.note: Exact-name collision with records in other federations or on the RSPWF lists; no document on these pages ties any of them to this wing. Kept distinct under the no-merge default, open to a merge on evidence.

name: Lifetaker

tenures.note: A former World champion; his ScraPreview flash is from a doctor's office, where he says his left knee will end his career after one more match, against Centris in a cage.

caption: A former World champion with a failing left knee who set his last match against Centris in a cage.

name: Centris

tenures.note: A former champion, as the clip show says of both men in the cage match; Jon Grey says Lifetaker is out to rid the league of him and the commentators call him a fluke winner; the Probing SCRA hears he may be taking a leave of absence after the cage match.

caption: The Beyonder whom Lifetaker wanted gone from the league in a Rasslefest cage match.

name: Rock Bottom Robbie

tenures.note: Holds the TV Title that Pablo Morales and Silver Stone challenged him for at Rasslefest; the clip show has him take it from Morales with the Rock Bottom Slam, and he defends it against Doug Adams on 19 January 1998.

caption: The TV champion who took the title from Pablo Morales with the Rock Bottom Slam.

name: Pablo Morales

tenures.role: wrestler; former TV champion, partner of Stanlee Maxx
tenures.note: A high flyer who beat Green Knight for the TV Title and lost it to Rock Bottom Robbie; Stanlee Maxx calls him his "real partner and true friend" and he trains with him for Rasslefest.

caption: The aerial former TV champion who is Stanlee Maxx's partner.

identity.note: Exact-name collision with records in other federations or on the RSPWF lists; no document on these pages ties any of them to this wing. Kept distinct under the no-merge default, open to a merge on evidence.

name: Silver Stone

tenures.role: wrestler; a former North American champion
tenures.note: A former North American champion the panel calls fading; his ScraPreview flash is from Carson City, Nevada, where he promises to return to his old training schedule and take the TV Title.

caption: A fading former North American champion who went into the TV title match promising a return to his glory days.

name: Gangsta Impasse

tenures.role: wrestler; former North American champion, with John Drake
tenures.note: Hit Poink with Gangsta Impact; Johnny Destiny took the North American title from him with Stanlee Maxx's interference; his ScraPreview flash promises Maxx a New York Street Fight with all the weapons they can find.

caption: A street fighter and former North American champion who knocked out Poink with Gangsta Impact at Fatal Fall.

name: John Drake

tenures.note: Introduces himself with Gangsta Impasse as the Notorious Killaz; in the Boiler Room Brawl he hits Stanlee Maxx with the principal's stuffed dog.

caption: Gangsta Impasse's partner in the Notorious Killaz.

name: Stanlee Maxx

tenures.role: wrestler; formerly Poink, the Evil Cop Clown
tenures.note: Appears on 3 November 1997 declaring "POINK IS DEAD" and, in the clip show's words, "replacing his former appearance as Poink"; on 1 December he burns his police uniforms at ringside. The Free for All commentators set him against Gangsta Impasse in a New York Street Fight.

caption: A New Yorker who dropped the Poink cop-clown gimmick on 3 November 1997 and fought Gangsta Impasse at Rasslefest.

name: Reverend Aristotle Jones

tenures.note: Derek Mota calls him a 240-pound ground fighter who has "no right" to a cruiserweight title; the panel notes Jones relies on a mat style.

caption: A 240-pound mat wrestler whose place among the cruiserweights Derek Mota disputed.

name: "Cowboy" Ken Curtis

tenures.note: A technical brawler gunning for the World title whom J.W. Hardin tracked to SCRA; he answers Hardin's debut speech by charging the ring and calls him a washed-up old-timer.

At Blood, Sweat, and Tears (9 August 1998): introduced as the second special enforcer, he came out to Lynyrd Skynyrd's "Gimme Back My Bullets" in black tights, a vest and a flat-crowned hat with a bullrope and stared down Stonebreaker; during the grudge match he threw Steve Spector and Simon Lebec back into the ring; after it he cleared the ring with a chair, shook hands with Stonebreaker and hit him with the chair, then told the crowd he lives about three hours south, was hired by Ronnie D, who called him after the EMWC did, for money and no commitment, that he was there to keep the bayou boy in line, and that he will stay to see what floats to the top.

caption: The Cowboy, whom J.W. Hardin came to SCRA to fight.

identity.note: A 1998 Brawlers-poll entry with no federation and a 2017 UPW rumble entrant billed as a returning legend; neither names SCRA. Pending a verdict.
A bare 1998 Top 100 Brawlers placing under the plain name, no fed named. Name collision only; no document names both records, so they stay two, pending a verdict.
A 2017 Ultimate Rumble entrant billed as a returning legend. Name collision only; no document names both records, so they stay two, pending a verdict.

name: Anthony Logan

tenures.note: Wore a mask as Silverblade and unmasked on 17 November as Aladdin Style's brother; he broke Style's knee and then Jason Gore's with the heart punch, and faces Style in the Dog Collar match.

At An Evening To The Extreme (30 September 1998, Tokyo Dome), part two: ran in with Aladdin Style after the Bloodstorm match, dropped Bobby Storm and El Vampyro with the Dragonstrike Heart Punch (the narration calls him the psychotic martial arts master, looking on expressionlessly), took the microphone and told the Fraternity Boys that the illusion they are the greatest tandem alive is about to come to a rest, that their suspension seems a godsend but is temporary, and that being the last team standing in a sixteen-team tournament does not make them the best if the best were not invited.

caption: Silverblade, who unmasked as Aladdin Style's brother and crippled Style's knee and then Jason Gore's.

name: Aladdin Style

tenures.role: wrestler; the Golden King, half of the House of Lords
tenures.note: Half of the House of Lords with Jason Gore; his knee was destroyed by his brother Anthony Logan, forcing him to a mat style; after Gore's injury he announces he is walking alone, and on 19 January 1998 he calls himself the number seven contender.

At An Evening To The Extreme (30 September 1998, Tokyo Dome), part two: with his brother Anthony Logan he ran into the ring after the Bloodstorm match and took the microphone from Logan to a heel pop: 'We're back!'; he told the Down Boys the World Tag Titles could wait, that the House of Lords were looking for their old friends the Fraternity Boys, and recalled their pay per view match in which the Fraternity Boys kept the titles and the House of Lords won the clean pinfall at just over twelve minutes; the crowd remembers the short tour the Lords made a few months earlier; he stomped the fallen Bloodstorm and they left to 'New Orleans is Sinking' amid boos.

caption: The Golden King, who went solo after his brother wrecked his partner Jason Gore's knee.

name: Jason Gore

tenures.role: wrestler; Lord Jason Gore, half of the House of Lords
tenures.note: Aladdin Style's adopted brother and tag partner; Anthony Logan's heart punch hurt his knee in the match the clip show replays, and Style announces he "will never wrestle again".

At An Evening To The Extreme (7 October 1998, Palacio de los Deportes): the narration has the House of Lords appear in the aisleway with their manager "Lord" Jason Gore, and Todd Michaelson jokes that the team is 'Led to the ring by Al Gore'; the Lords then beat Anarchy by pinfall amid a swarm of Anarchy's fans, the Vogon Poet's Guild, after which the fans of Greece riot with the Guild.

caption: Aladdin Style's adopted brother and partner, whose knee was ruined.

name: Johnny Destiny

tenures.role: wrestler; the Crazy Canuck, North American champion
tenures.note: Nathan Flash's adopted brother and longtime partner; Flash attacked him on crutches at Fatal Fall, and Destiny returned to win the North American title from Gangsta Impasse; on 19 January 1998 Flash says the SCRA cut off his contract.

caption: The Crazy Canuck, whom his adopted brother Nathan Flash turned on and crippled before Rasslefest.

name: Nathan Flash

tenures.role: wrestler; North American champion until 19 January 1998
tenures.note: Turned on Johnny Destiny at Fatal Fall, beat him at Rasslefest for the North American title, then on 19 January 1998 threw the belt down, said he quit and asked his "brother" to come home.

caption: Johnny Destiny's adopted brother, who won the North American title from him and quit on 19 January 1998.

name: Eddy "Flap" Jacks

tenures.role: wrestler; World champion, House of Pancakes
tenures.note: The "behemoth World champ" of the recruitment call; the clip show has him hit Lucifer with Pancake Poison at the side of Klondike and bring out the House of Pancakes, and his ScraPreview flash promises to take Lucifer the full 60.

caption: The World champion who answered Lucifer with the House of Pancakes.

identity.note: The registry's Eddy ("Flap") Jacks entries are poll placings (1998 Brawlers, no federation; 2000 Top 200, tagged 'Many'); none names SCRA. Pending a verdict.

name: Lucifer

tenures.role: wrestler; the Dark One, a Pit of Damnation member
tenures.note: Won a title shot at Fatal Fall; Eddy Jacks hurt him with the House of Pancakes on 27 October; the Probing SCRA hears Rasslefest may be his last match.

caption: A brawler whose World title shot against Eddy Jacks at Rasslefest may be his last match.

identity.note: A stock demonic ring name carried in many federations; nothing on these pages ties SCRA's Dark One to any of the live namesakes, nor to the MLWO and NTICW Lucifers (lucifer-mlwo-1998, lucifer-nticw-2000). Kept distinct under the no-merge default.

name: Kil Jaeden

tenures.note: Is knocked out with a chair by two hooded men at Onset of Fury while Lucifer wrestles Lifetaker in the ring; the clip show calls Lucifer his mentor, and he lifts his "master" in victory.

caption: Lucifer's protege, laid out with a chair at Onset of Fury.

name: Klondike

tenures.note: One of the Pancakers beside Eddy Jacks, shown throwing Gangsta Impasse into Jacks's powerslam and putting on the Klondike clutch.

caption: The Pancaker who works beside Eddy Jacks.

name: Nik Nyce

tenures.note: Debuts on 19 January 1998 as "The Perfectionist" at 234 pounds from Chicago and loses the opener to Bobby McAllister, pinned out of a DDT while setting up Standing Nycely.

caption: The Perfectionist, a 234-pound Chicagoan whom Bobby McAllister pinned in his debut.

identity.note: This wing's commentators bill him as 'The Perfectionist' who 'has held titles all around the world'; the registry's 'The Perfectionist' Nik Nyce records (AWA and SJPW 1997, TPW 1997, IEWF/LWC 1997, IIEW 1998) share the billing, but no document names this wing, no vitals are recorded on them to compare, and the registry has not joined them to each other. Pending a verdict.

name: Bobby McAllister

tenures.note: Debuts on 19 January 1998 at 224 lbs with Victoria Glenn, to the Marine Hymn, and pins Nik Nyce with a DDT out of a counter.

caption: A 224-pound debutant who upset Nik Nyce with a DDT on 19 January 1998.

name: Zak Rage

tenures.note: Named "arguably the best flyer in SCRA"; the clip show shows him win the tag titles for the Activists with a springboard missile dropkick and a hurricarana on 1 December.

caption: The aerial half of the Activists from Hell.

name: Joshua Baker

tenures.note: Won the 17 November pep-rally match and so a title shot, and tags Zak Rage in on 1 December for the Activists' tag title win.

caption: The partner of Zak Rage, who won the pep-rally match that earned the Activists their title shot.

name: Bill Baer

tenures.note: Called "William" by Tulkas Naugrim, a power man whose strength gives the Guard an edge in the ladder match.

caption: The power man of the Praetorian Guard.

name: Tulkas Naugrim

tenures.note: Speaks in archaic English and rolls up Aladdin Style on 10 November for the Guard's tag title win.

caption: The archaic-spoken half of the Praetorian Guard.

name: Tavis

tenures.role: wrestler; a former member of the Pros
tenures.note: Was knocked out by Joseph Eagle's chair at Fatal Fall on 12 October; Grant says he left for California after Miss Frank was seen with the Eagles.

caption: The Pros member who left for California after the German Eagles took Miss Frank.

name: Grant

tenures.role: wrestler; a member of the Pros
tenures.note: Tavis's partner, called "Mr. Grant", now teamed with Walt Jabasco; his ScraPreview flash says the German Eagles are all he can think of.

caption: The Pros member who stayed and teamed with Walt Jabasco.

tenures.role: wrestler; a member of the Pros
tenures.note: Grant's new partner in the reconfigured Pros; his ScraPreview flash has him slingshot a masked opponent into a flying clothesline.

caption: Grant's new partner in the reconfigured Pros.

name: Joseph Eagle

tenures.note: At Fatal Fall he nailed Tavis with a chair meant for Gore, costing the Pros the belts.

caption: The German Eagle whose chair cost the Pros the tag titles at Fatal Fall.

name: Allen Jenkins

tenures.role: wrestler; half of Phi Theta Kappa
tenures.note: Burned when the Angels of Darkness set his toga alight; the clip shows his hair gone and second-degree burns on his calves.

caption: Half of Phi Theta Kappa, burned by the Angels of Darkness.

name: Brad Thompson

tenures.role: wrestler; half of Phi Theta Kappa
tenures.note: Vows with Jenkins to avenge the fire and tells the Creator they have worse plans for him.

caption: Half of Phi Theta Kappa, who vowed revenge for the fire.

name: Carnage

tenures.role: wrestler; half of the Angels of Darkness
tenures.note: Conjures a fireball and tells Phi Theta Kappa that "Play with fire and you get burned".

caption: Half of the Angels of Darkness, who held out a fireball to threaten Phi Theta Kappa.

tenures.note: Calls Carnage his brother and the Creator his father.

tenures.note: Waves a Soviet flag at the fans and takes the Express's punishment before Dragovich pins him.

caption: Half of Cold Winter, who waved a Soviet flag to the boos.

tenures.note: Ignores the crowd in his light blue ring attire and is chokeslammed and gorilla-pressed by Bolotov.

caption: Half of Cold Winter, in light blue ring attire.

tenures.note: Taken out by the Siberian Express at the start of the three-way.

caption: A Malaysian Star, eliminated first.

tenures.note: Left for Cold Winter after Fox falls, pinned with his partner in no time.

caption: A Malaysian Star, pinned in the opening seconds.

name: Chris Eagle

tenures.role: wrestler; a German Eagle, Joseph Eagle's brother
tenures.note: Billed from Trier, Germany at 240 pounds with his brother and tag team partner Joseph Eagle and their manager Ocki the Moselman; a high flyer who hit an asai moonsault on Walt Jabasco on 26 January 1998 and pinned Grant after the Double German Suplex to win the tag titles for the German Eagles.

caption: The high-flying half of the German Eagles, who pinned Grant to win the tag titles on 26 January 1998.

name: Ocki the Moselman

tenures.note: Walks out ahead of the German Eagles waving a German flag, as he did at Onset of Fury; on 26 January 1998 the Eagles come out, for the first time in months, accompanied by him.

caption: The Moselman who walks the German Eagles to the ring.

name: Lon Savarese

tenures.note: One of Eddy Jacks's managers (billed Lon Saverese at Onset of Fury): he talks strategy with Jacks on the way to the ring and is run over by Jacks with Surefoot on 19 January 1998.

caption: One of Eddy Jacks's managers, who walked him to the ring for the World title match of 19 January 1998.

name: Tain Surefoot

tenures.note: One of Eddy Jacks's managers: he jars it up with a group of fans beside Bill Baer on the way to the ring on 26 January 1998, and Jacks runs him over with Savarese in the World title match of 19 January.

caption: One of Eddy Jacks's managers, run over by Jacks in the World title match of 19 January 1998.

name: Mal Epstein

tenures.note: Walks out with Sgt. Pepper and the Lonely Hearts Club Band, as he did at Fatal Fall, where he threw Doink off Pepper, and on 26 January 1998.

caption: Sgt. Pepper's companion, who comes to the ring beside the Lonely Hearts Club Band.

name: Penelope Lane

tenures.note: Walks out with Sgt. Pepper on 15 December 1997, slapping the fans' hands as they go, and again on 26 January 1998, when she and Mal Epstein accompany him to the ring for the TV title match.

caption: Sgt. Pepper's companion, who walks to the ring beside him.

name: "Latexman" Art Vandilay

tenures.note: Already in the ring when the Scraps of 26 January 1998 opens with an unannounced match; Phantom attacks him from behind and pins him while Chase Hunter is entertaining the commentators. Jack Hazard calls such wrestlers jobbers.

caption: A jobber pinned by Phantom in the unannounced opener of 26 January 1998.

name: Chase Hunter

tenures.role: newcomer under contract; guest at the commentary desk
tenures.note: Walks down to the commentary desk on 26 January 1998, trades insults with Jack Hazard and mimics a gothic wrestler around the ring while Phantom wrestles; Jon Grey then reports that he is a new member of SCRA under contract, and Hazard later tries out insults on him.

caption: A cocky newcomer who heckled Jack Hazard at the commentary desk on 26 January 1998 before it was announced he is under contract.

identity.note: The registry's Chase Hunter is a placing in the RSPWF Top 200 for 1999 tagged UWF, with no document; nothing ties it to this wing's newcomer of January 1998. Kept distinct under the no-merge default, open to a merge on evidence.

name: Wellington

tenures.note: Referees Aladdin Style against Prodigy on 19 January 1998: Prodigy asks for a quicker count and Wellington waves off a three-count, saying Style got his shoulder up.

caption: The referee of Aladdin Style against Prodigy on 19 January 1998.

name: Hans Foresmits

tenures.note: Referees J.W. Hardin against Derek Mota on 19 January 1998; he rings the bell for a submission and Tommy Gregory later says he did so under false pretense.

caption: The referee who called Hardin's win over Derek Mota on 19 January 1998 before it was overruled.

name: Shooter McNutty

tenures.role: one of Gangsta Impasse's party at the barn
tenures.note: Seen in the video of 2 February 1998 with Street Smarts and Tommy Gregory beside Gangsta Impasse and John Drake while they rake horse manure in Ken Curtis's barn; he cocks his finger at Street Smarts, helps trash the barn and leaves with Impasse's party in Impasse's car. Jon Grey replays the footage in the ScraPreview of 7 February.

caption: One of the men who helped Gangsta Impasse trash Ken Curtis's barn in the video of 2 February 1998.

name: Street Smarts

tenures.note: Leaves the barn for a potty break in the video of 2 February 1998, then drives Gangsta Impasse's red Benz through the barnyard door and hits Tommy Gregory; Impasse thanks him ('you ma man') and he joins the wrecking of the barn. The ScraPreview of 7 February replays the footage.

caption: The driver who put Gangsta Impasse's Benz through Ken Curtis's barn door and into Tommy Gregory.

name: Crow

tenures.role: the man who carried Tommy Gregory out of the burning barn
tenures.note: In the barn footage shown on 7 February 1998 a man in jeans and sneakers, no shirt, appears from nowhere, runs into the burning barn and comes out carrying Tommy Gregory over his shoulder; Jack Hazard afterwards calls him 'Crow' and a certified hero.

caption: The shirtless stranger who carried Tommy Gregory out of Ken Curtis's burning barn.

identity.note: Four registry records are called Crow (LOW, NCCW, FWG, SXW); none names the SCRA, and this Crow is a man glimpsed in a single burning-barn clip. Kept distinct under the no-merge default.

name: Jack Slaton

tenures.role: with Bobby McAllister at the Penn State gym
tenures.note: Walks into the gym where Bobby McAllister records his ScraPreview flash on 7 February 1998 and tells him it is time to catch his flight, Victoria Glenn already at the airport; McAllister names him beside Victoria Glenn as someone he fights for.

caption: The man who walks Bobby McAllister out of the Penn State gym to his flight.

name: Sengir

tenures.role: wrestler; a battle royal entrant with Jezra Wagner at his side
tenures.note: Shown arriving with Jezra Wagner at the Silver Swan hotel on 7 February 1998, in a suite the SCRA officials have paid for; Jon Grey gives him little chance in the Winter Carnival battle royal because of his size. The same hotel scene, with the EMWC in place of the SCRA, stands on the live EMWC page of 9 March 1998.
At An Evening To The Extreme (9 March 1998): shown arriving with Jezra Wagner at the Silver Swan hotel in an EMWC-paid suite; the announcers named him as soon to make his EMWC debut.

Debuted in a dark match on 4 September, beating Enrique Valasquez with a finisher he calls "The Setting Sun"; lost to "Malicious" Mike Hrankiwskyj on Monday Night Battlezone on 14 September and was beaten down with brass knuckles after the bell, managed to the ring by "The Ice Queen" Jezra Wagner; beat Burden in a dark match on 11 September, then was beaten down by Burden after the bell; failed to appear for a scheduled 28 September bout, and President Hopper terminated his contract on-air, awarding the match to his opponent.

caption: A wrestler shown checking into the Silver Swan hotel with Jezra Wagner ahead of the Winter Carnival.

name: Jezra Wagner

tenures.note: Walks into the Silver Swan hotel with Sengir on 7 February 1998 and gives the receptionist her name as Jez Wagner; in the lift she teases the young bellhop.
At An Evening To The Extreme (9 March 1998): shown arriving with Sengir at the Silver Swan hotel, identifying herself to the clerk as Jez Wagner.
Sengir's valet; clashed with backstage reporter Dyan Cicarelli outside Sengir's locker room before his on-air debut, and was restrained by Sengir from attacking her.

caption: Sengir's companion at the Silver Swan hotel, who calls herself Jez Wagner.

name: Sir John Caboto

tenures.note: Stands at ringside beside the Haida Warrior Gwaii Edenshaw as the ring is set for the Winter Carnival on 7 February 1998, tells the Haida creation story of Raven and the clamshell and promises that the Warrior will beat Chase Hunter.

caption: The ringside storyteller who spoke for the Haida Warrior Gwaii Edenshaw.

name: "Haida Warrior" Gwaii Edenshaw

tenures.role: wrestler; a newcomer entered in the battle royal
tenures.note: Billed the Haida Warrior; Jon Grey asks Chase Hunter about a newcomer who has said nasty things about his past and names him, and Sir John Caboto promises on 7 February 1998 that the Warrior will look for Hunter first in the Winter Carnival battle royal. Jon Grey gives him an outside shot, with size and animal instincts against inexperience.

caption: A newcomer billed the Haida Warrior, who made Chase Hunter his first target for the Winter Carnival battle royal.

name: "Hot Stuff" Mike Justice

tenures.note: Seen on a treadmill in the SCRA training facility on 7 February 1998, flexing for the camera, saying he expects 'little boys like Nik Nyce and Chase Hunter' to try to hurt him in the battle royal and warning the 'girly boys' of a bad weekend; Jon Grey gives him an outside chance on size.

caption: The self-styled sexiest man in the SCRA, an SCRA rookie sensation entered in the Winter Carnival.

identity.note: The registry's "Apostle" Mike Justice is a placing in the RSPWF Top 200 for 2000 tagged EMWC, with no document; he carries a different nickname and no document ties him to this wing's rookie. Kept distinct under the no-merge default, open to a merge on evidence.

name: "The Iconoclast" Sean Watts

tenures.role: wrestler; entered in the battle royal
tenures.note: Previewed by Jon Grey and Jack Hazard on 7 February 1998 as 'the enigma of the league', who seems not to care about matches and puts himself down; he has no flash of his own in the preview.

caption: The league's enigma, previewed as a long shot for the Winter Carnival battle royal.

identity.note: The registry's "Iconoclast" Sean Watts is a placing in the RSPWF Top 100 Cruisers for 1998 with no federation named beside it and no document; it shares the name and billing of this wing's Iconoclast, but nothing ties the two (as with Eddy Jacks and Eddy "Flap" Jacks). The CCW 1997 record ('Sensational' Sean Watts) shares only the name. The Neo Alberta 2000 record is billed 'The Iconoclast', from UWF, in October 2002: a lead to be read with the UWF lineage, not a merge; nothing on these pages ties this wing's Iconoclast to it. Kept distinct pending a verdict.

name: Pony Express

tenures.role: wrestler; the mystery man of the battle royal
tenures.note: The cowboy-hatted mystery man of the preview of 7 February 1998, whose identity is to be revealed at the Winter Carnival; he says he will be there whether the president lets him in or not, with his boys behind him, and is shown jumped by a carload of well-dressed 'Socs' and rescued by four 'Greasers'.

tenures.role: wrestler; a newcomer who crashed the singles battle royal
tenures.note: Heard on the arena PA during the singles battle royal of 8 February 1998 as a shadow on the big screen, saying he has watched the league for a couple of weeks and is ready to 'kick some ass'; he names himself Ponyboy Kertins and says 'most people know me as being Golden, but thats a whole other story'. He then jumps the guardrail, hits Phantom with a hurricarrana from the top rope and later eliminates him with a dropkick, helps Prodigy against Rock Bottom Robbie, and goes out when Bobby McAllister's forearm bounces Nik Nyce into him. Jack Hazard: 'Who the hell is this Ponyboy?' and 'I thought we were going for some big name star and we get this runt?'

caption: The hat-brimmed mystery man who promised to crash the Winter Carnival with his boys.

identity.note: The registry's Pony Express is an unnamed tag team in a December 1999 house show of ACWA Atlantic; it shares only the name with this wing's mystery man. Kept distinct under the no-merge default.

name: Comrade Zangief

tenures.role: wrestler; one half of Comrades Inc.
tenures.note: Introduced on 8 February 1998 by Comrade Jonah Ulanov as one of the 'very big men' of Comrades Inc., 'not mean men'; he sends a message to the German Eagles, saying he is part German and will have to beat them up because they are not with Comrades Inc., and when the float tips over he is the one who has to be pulled up, his hair so heavy he cannot swim. He then admits he filled the pool with gasoline. On 9 February he lifts Chris Eagle with ease and spins him into a piledriver (Jon Grey: 'The Russian Spinning Piledriver') during the Activists from Hell's title match; Jack Hazard calls him the Russian Wrecker.

caption: The big Russian of Comrades Inc., who piledrove Chris Eagle in the title match of 9 February 1998.

name: Comrade Johnstone

tenures.role: wrestler; one half of Comrades Inc.
tenures.note: Answers Comrade Jonah Ulanov's 'That right Comrade Johnstone?' through the speech of 8 February 1998 with 'That right Comrade Jonah!', and explains the team's plan to beat up everyone in the SCRA. On 9 February he climbs onto the ring apron in the Activists from Hell's title match and smashes a Russian flag over Chris Eagle's head.

caption: The Comrades Inc. man who hit Chris Eagle with a Russian flag.

name: Comrade Jonah Ulanov

tenures.note: Opens the Comrades Inc. segment of 8 February 1998 with 'Peoples of SCRA lend me your ears' and speaks for the team; he clicks the lighter that sets the gasoline-filled pool, and the ring, on fire. On 9 February he climbs the top rope to distract the referee while his team attacks Chris Eagle, jumps down from the apron waving the Ukraine flag and sits at the announce desk to say they kicked the German Eagles.

caption: The man who speaks for Comrades Inc. and distracted the referee for them.

name: Oscar

tenures.role: wrestler; one of the Weenie Machines
tenures.note: One of the two Weenie Machines in the tag team battle royal of 8 February 1998: Bill Baer attacks both Weenie Machines at the bell and eliminates him at once, leaving his brother Mayer alone.

caption: A Weenie Machine thrown out of the tag battle royal by Bill Baer.

name: Mayer

tenures.role: wrestler; one of the Weenie Machines
tenures.note: The other Weenie Machine, hiding in the corner while his brother Oscar is eliminated, then eliminating Icelander, Brad Thompson and Tulkas Naugrim in the tag team battle royal of 8 February 1998 (the 'Weenification' half-move named by Jon Grey) before Andrei Bolotov gorilla presses him over the top into a snow bank.

caption: The Weenie Machine who eliminated three men in the tag battle royal before Andrei Bolotov threw him out.

name: Darry

tenures.role: one of the Greasers, Ponyboy Kertins's entourage
tenures.note: One of the four Greasers who lead Ponyboy Kertins to the ring in the four-way dance of 16 February 1998. He goes into the ring right away while the others climb the apron, takes a corner when the Greasers pose, and stands cross-armed beside Cherry with Two-Bit as the fireworks go off; the referee, Wellington, has the non-wrestlers leave the ring before the bell.

caption: A Greaser who led Ponyboy Kertins down the ramp on 16 February 1998.

name: Soda

tenures.role: one of the Greasers, Ponyboy Kertins's entourage
tenures.note: One of the four Greasers at Ponyboy Kertins's side on 16 February 1998. He walks on the ring apron while Darry goes into the ring, and kneels flexing beside Kertins when the Greasers pose, and leaves the ring when Wellington orders the non-wrestlers out.

caption: A Greaser who flexed beside Ponyboy Kertins on 16 February 1998.

name: Two-Bit

tenures.role: one of the Greasers, Ponyboy Kertins's entourage
tenures.note: One of the four Greasers who bring Ponyboy Kertins to the ring on 16 February 1998. He plays around with the fans' hands on the way down in his Mickey Mouse shirt and stands cross-armed beside Cherry with Darry when the Greasers pose.

caption: A Greaser in a Mickey Mouse shirt who came to the ring with Ponyboy Kertins on 16 February 1998.

name: Steve

tenures.role: one of the Greasers, Ponyboy Kertins's entourage
tenures.note: One of the four Greasers at Ponyboy Kertins's side on 16 February 1998. He follows Soda onto the ring apron and kneels flexing on Kertins's other side when the Greasers pose, as the fireworks go off.

caption: A Greaser who posed beside Ponyboy Kertins on 16 February 1998.

name: Cherry

tenures.role: walks to the ring with Ponyboy Kertins and the Greasers
tenures.note: Named on 7 February 1998 in the clip in which the Socs jump the mystery man in the black cowboy hat: as they hold him down, one of them tells him 'Dis is fer stealin' Cherry.' On 16 February 1998 Cherry, in a red miniskirt, comes down the ramp with Ponyboy Kertins and the Greasers; Kertins opens the ropes for Cherry, and Darry and Two-Bit stand cross-armed on either side of Cherry when the Greasers pose.

caption: Came to the ring in a red miniskirt with Ponyboy Kertins and the Greasers on 16 February 1998; a week earlier a Soc had told the mystery man 'Dis is fer stealin' Cherry.'
